extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners (persons preparing or processing Information Disclosure Statements)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner guidance for preparing, filing, and handling Information Disclosure Statements (IDSs) during U.S. patent prosecution, including timing, content, signature, copies, non-English documents, and treatment in continuing/national-stage proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological sequence listing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications that disclose nucleic acid and/or amino acid sequences (as defined in 37 CFR 1.821(a) for applications filed before July 1, 2022 or 37 CFR 1.831(b) for applications filed on or after July 1, 2022) are required to provide the biological sequence information in a sequence listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed before July 1, 2022: submit a Sequence Listing as an ASCII plain text file in compliance with 37 CFR 1.821-1.824 via USPTO electronic filing system or read-only optical disc (see MPEP §§ 2420 et seq.). For applications filed on or after July 1, 2022: submit a Sequence Listing XML in compliance with 37 CFR 1.831-1.834 via USPTO electronic filing system or read-only optical disc (see MPEP §§ 2412-2419).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing requirements for IDS filing (37 CFR 1.97)
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS will be considered by the Office only if filed within specified time frames in 37 CFR 1.97(b)-(d) or if filed later but accompanied by required statements/fees set out in 1.97(c)-(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted timing windows include: (1) within three months of the filing date for national applications (other than CPAs) or before first Office action on the merits, whichever is later; (2) within three months of entry of national stage or before first Office action on the merits; (3) before mailing of a first Office action on the merits; (4) before mailing of first Office action after filing an RCE; (5) within three months of publication of international registration in an international design application. IDSs filed after these windows may be considered if filed before final action/notice of allowance/closing prosecution and accompanied by a 1.97(e) statement or 1.17(p) fee, or in certain situations up to payment of the issue fee with both statement and fee. No extensions under 1.136 are permitted except limited relief when a bona fide attempt was made to comply (see 1.97(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.97(e) statement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When required under 37 CFR 1.97, a signed statement must accompany an IDS specifying either that each item was first cited in a communication from a foreign patent office in a counterpart foreign application not more than three months prior to filing, or that no item was so cited and, after reasonable inquiry, was not known to any individual designated in 37 CFR 1.56(c) more than three months prior to filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement must be signed (see 1.33(b) requirements). The specific language and certifications required by 1.97(e) must be used; failure to provide the statement when required will prevent the IDS from being considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirement (37 CFR 1.33(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS must be signed in compliance with 37 CFR 1.33(b) (e.g., a separate signed page which references and accompanies the IDS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An electronic IDS (eIDS) submission in compliance with the Legal Framework for Patent Electronic System (MPEP § 502.03) satisfies the signature requirement. Ensure a properly signed page accompanies the IDS unless eIDS signature methods are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirement — list of all cited information (37 CFR 1.98(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each IDS must include a list of all patents, publications, U.S. applications, or other information submitted for consideration by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.98(a)(1) prescribes the format: U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications must be listed in a section separate from other documents; each page must identify the application number of the application in which the IDS is submitted (if known); include a column beside each document for examiner initials; and have a heading that clearly indicates the list is an Information Disclosure Statement. Use PTO/SB/08 to comply easily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification requirements for cited documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Each cited document in an IDS must be properly identified using the specific identifiers required by 37 CFR 1.98(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: U.S. patents by inventor, patent number, and issue date; U.S. patent application publications by applicant, publication number, and publication date; U.S. applications by inventor, application number, and filing date; foreign patent documents by country/patent office, document number, and publication/issue date; publications by publisher, author (if any), title, relevant pages, date and place of publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies requirement for cited non-U.S. and non-stored items (37 CFR 1.98(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Legible copies are required for certain cited items in order for them to be considered by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required copies include: (i) each cited foreign patent; (ii) each cited publication or the portion that caused listing (other than U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications unless the Office requires them); (iii) for each cited pending unpublished U.S. application, the application specification including the claims and any drawings, or the portion which caused it to be listed (unless the cited pending U.S. application is stored in IFW); and (iv) all other cited information or the portion which caused listing. Failure to provide required copies will cause the IDS not to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-English document handling
rubrics_metrics.description: For cited non-English documents, provide either a concise explanation of the relevance (as presently understood by the individual in 37 CFR 1.56(c) most knowledgeable about the content) and/or a written English-language translation if in the signatory’s possession, custody, control, or readily available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The concise explanation may be separate from the specification or incorporated therein. If a full translation is available in the possession or control of a designated individual, submit the translation. See MPEP § 609.04(a) for detailed requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS considered only if procedural and content requirements satisfied
rubrics_metrics.description: To have an IDS considered by the Office during pendency, it must (1) comply with 37 CFR 1.98 content requirements, (2) be filed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.97 timing/procedural requirements, and (3) be signed per 37 CFR 1.33(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an IDS does not comply with these rules it will be placed in the file but not considered. A bona fide attempt with inadvertent omissions may permit additional time to supply missing content (see 1.97(f) and MPEP guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner handling and marking of IDS citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must review IDSs for compliance and then consider properly submitted information in the same manner as other Office search file documents; they must indicate consideration or lack thereof on the listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner actions include initialing the blank column next to a citation or using the electronic alternative by inserting the phrase “All references considered except where lined through” with electronic initials and signature on the final page; drawing a line through citations not considered and informing applicant why; writing “not considered” if none comply and using form paragraphs 6.49 et seq.; signing and dating the IDS listing and ensuring a signed copy is entered into the file and mailed to applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS is not a representation of a search or admission of materiality
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of an IDS shall not be construed as a representation that any patentability search has been made, nor as an admission that the information cited is material to patentability as defined in 37 CFR 1.56(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.97(g) and 1.97(h) and MPEP § 2129 regarding admissions by applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party submission limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Third parties (not covered by 37 CFR 1.56(c)) cannot file IDSs under 37 CFR 1.97/1.98; they may submit patents and publications under 37 CFR 1.290 in published applications or may file a protest under 37 CFR 1.291 for unpublished pending applications before allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party submissions must comply with 1.290 or 1.291; noncompliant third‑party submissions will not be entered into the application file and will be discarded. Office personnel will not act on third‑party inquiries except when in compliance with those rules; oral or telephone comments from third parties are declined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple IDSs allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: More than one IDS may be filed in a single application; each will be considered provided it complies with the appropriate requirements of 37 CFR 1.97, 1.98, and 1.33(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of PTO/SB/08 is encouraged for each IDS to give a uniform listing and to enable examiner notation and OCR processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PTO/SB/08 form recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are encouraged to use the USPTO form PTO/SB/08, 'Information Disclosure Statement,' to prepare IDSs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTO/SB/08 provides a separate section for U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications and the required columns and headings; the form is updated by the Office and facilitates compliance and OCR. Do not submit PTO/SB/08 or PTO-892 forms copied from other applications (they may contain other application numbers or examiner initials that will confuse records).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative disclosures allowance (when multiple disclosures are substantively cumulative)
rubrics_metrics.description: When disclosures of two or more patents or publications listed in an IDS are substantively cumulative, a copy of one of the patents or publications may be submitted without copies of the other patents or publications provided it is stated that the other patents/publications are cumulative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows avoiding redundant copies, but the IDS must state which items are cumulative. See 37 CFR 1.98(c) guidance in MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission rules in continuing, CPA, CIP, and RCE contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Information considered in a parent application will generally be part of the file before the examiner in certain continuing applications (CPAs, continuation, divisional, CIP) and will not need resubmission unless applicant desires the information to be printed on the patent or other specific circumstances apply; if resubmitted, the listing must comply with 37 CFR 1.98(a)(1) format and 1.97 timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For CPAs filed under 1.53(d), information considered in the parent need not be resubmitted. For continuation/divisional/CIP under 1.53(b), the examiner will consider information considered in the parent; resubmission is not required unless applicant wants it printed on the patent. When resubmitting, do not submit PTO/SB/08 or PTO‑892 copies from other applications; provide a new listing complying with format and timing. IDSs filed before an RCE that comply with 1.98 will be considered after filing the RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: National stage (PCT) IDS handling and printing-on-patent requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In PCT national stage applications, the examiner will consider U.S. patents, U.S. patent application publications, and U.S. pending applications cited in the international search report that are stored in the USPTO Image File Wrapper (IFW); other documents cited in the international search report will be considered only when the national-stage file indicates copies are present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations in the international search report are not themselves IDSs and will not be printed on the patent unless a separate listing complying with 37 CFR 1.98(a)(1) (preferably PTO/SB/08) is filed. If copies required by 1.98 are not present in the national-stage file, the burden is on applicant to supply them. Use form paragraphs (e.g., 6.53–6.55) as appropriate to notify applicant of consideration or lack thereof and any deadlines for submitting a compliant listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of noncompliance — placement vs. consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Information submitted that does not comply with 37 CFR 1.97, 1.98, or 1.33(b) will be placed in the application file but will not be considered by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners will strike through or mark citations not considered and inform applicant of reasons. If a bona fide attempt was made and content was inadvertently omitted, additional time may be allowed under 1.97(f) to enable full compliance (see MPEP § 609.04(b) and form paragraph 6.51).
